(u2, else) -> u2

(u1, top_breach | side_breach, u1) -> -1000
(u2, top_breach | side_breach, u1) -> -1000
feedback: The core breach-tracking is sound: every top_breach or side_breach moves the machine into the absorbing failure state u1 with a per-breach penalty, all states have exhaustive and mutually exclusive ordered transitions (the !top_breach & !side_breach guard on the kill transition correctly prevents nondeterminism when a kill and a breach co-occur on one step), per-state else self-loops cover the irrelevant plant_trampled event, the four propositions are used as one-step events with persistence carried by the state, no regression transitions are needed since a breach is irreversible, and FINAL_STATES is present and nonempty with u0 and u2 both meaning 'no breach yet', so the success semantics match the task. The candidate still fails on three counts. (1) Semantic fidelity / compactness: u2 records only 'at least one clean kill has happened', a distinction the task does not make. 'Preferably, no zombie gets through on any of the three lanes' is fully captured by a two-state no-breach/breached machine; the extra state, the one-off +1.0 crossing reward, and the redundant second final state are grounded in neither the task text nor the environment's per-kill reward, and violate compactness. (2) Progress density: the kill reward fires exactly once — (u0, zombie_killed & !breaches, u2) -> 1.0 is consumed by the first kill, and every later kill falls into (u2, else) with reward 0, even though killing is the only mechanism that prevents future breaches. Either reward every kill with a bounded amount in all no-breach states, or drop the kill machinery entirely; rewarding exactly one kill is not dense and is arbitrary. (3) Reward safety: -1000 per breach against a +1.0 progress reward is a 1000:1 scale mismatch; with roughly 18-37 zombies entering and late-episode breaches largely unavoidable, returns become large, high-variance negatives that drown the shaping channel and risk unstable learning — use a moderate bounded penalty consistent with the paper's reward convention. Minor note: when top_breach and side_breach co-occur on one step, the combined guard charges a single violation although two zombies got through; if the paper's reward semantics allow per-proposition charges on one label, the conjunction should be penalized separately.

feedback: Mechanically the artifact is in good shape: the paper-format headers are all present (STATES, INITIAL_STATE, and a nonempty FINAL_STATES listing the declared state u0, which is trivially reachable as the initial state and meaningfully accepting — ending in u0 is exactly the fully preferred outcome of zero breaches); transitions use only the four given event propositions; the u0 list is mutually exclusive, ordered specific-before-else, and exhaustive (the dedicated top_breach & side_breach entry correctly prices the same-step double breach this environment can produce, and a step with both a kill and a breach correctly resolves to the breach entry, so the kill is subordinate on shared steps); plant_trampled, the one irrelevant event, is absorbed by per-state else self-loops; all propositions are events and are consumed as one-shot edges rather than persistent guards; rewards are modest and bounded (−5/−10 per breach event, +0.1 per kill with ≤ ~37 kills per episode, and the kill bonus can never offset a breach penalty); equal top- and side-lane penalties are right here since the task disprefers all three lanes equally; and no regression transitions are needed because a breach is irreversible. The fatal defect is semantic fidelity of the soft constraint. 'Preferably, no zombie gets through on any of the three lanes' is a degree-sensitive preference: every breach is a fresh violation and fewer breaches is strictly better. The machine instead encodes a one-shot hard violation: u1 is an absorbing, reward-dead sink — (u1, else) -> u1 carries no reward — so after the first breach every further breach, including additional top-lane breaches, costs nothing, and zombie_killed stops paying. Both the −5 per-breach pricing and the +0.1 dense kill progress reward die at the first breach. This matters concretely: spawn pressure rises until 'more zombies come than the agent can stop', and even the reference guard run incurs four side breaches, so on essentially every realistic episode the machine goes mute for the episode tail, cannot distinguish one breach from thirty, and gives the agent no reason to keep killing or defending any lane. A hard 'never' template has been applied to a soft 'preferably' task. To be acceptable, per-occurrence accounting must survive the first breach while preserving the (correct) acceptance semantics that ending in the final state ⇔ no breach ever occurred: either charge every breach in the clean state via penalized self-loops (dropping u1), or mirror u0's breach penalties and kill reward in u1's outgoing transitions so the breached state keeps scoring instead of looping silently. Minor: the else transitions carry no explicit reward entries (implicit 0) — confirm the format defaults omitted rewards to zero, otherwise list them.

feedback: Accept. Format: the paper headers (REWARD_MACHINE, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, FINAL_STATES, TRANSITION_FUNCTION, REWARD_FUNCTION) are all present in order, arrows and reward triples are well formed, and every transition target is a declared state. FINAL_STATES is nonempty: u0 is declared and is the accepting state (the episode satisfies the preference iff the RM ends in u0, i.e., no breach ever occurred); u1 is reachable from u0 via the breach transitions, so reachability holds. Ordered transition coverage is correct in both states: the top_breach & side_breach conjunction precedes the single-breach rows, so a double-breach step deterministically pays -10 instead of being masked by a single-event row, and breach rows precede zombie_killed, so a kill coinciding with a breach cannot mask the penalty (the kill's +0.1 is simply not paid that step, which is deterministic and safe). Irrelevant events are handled as required: plant_trampled and empty steps fall into the per-state else self-loops with implicit zero reward, and plants are genuinely irrelevant to this zombie-only preference. All four propositions are one-step events used only as edge labels, so there is no persistent/event misuse. Reward safety and density: breaches are the only negative rewards and kills the only positive source; zombie entries are capped by the environment (18-37 per episode), so the +0.1 progress reward is dense (kills every ~14 steps under a good policy) yet bounded (<= ~3.7 per episode) and cannot be farmed; nothing rewards inducing a breach. Regressions: none are needed — the preference, once violated, stays violated for the episode, so the absorbing u1 with continued -5/-10 self-loop penalties is the right structure and it correctly grades multiple breaches (as in the example trace's repeated side breaches). Compactness: two states is minimal, a single memory bit distinguishing no-breach from breached, which is exactly what the accepting-state semantics require.
